 Oral Order
1.

The petitioners, who are facing charges for offences punishable under Sections 379, 338 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 3, 5, and 146 read with Sections 181, 180, and 196 of the
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, are before this Court.

2. The prosecution case is that the second respondent lodged a First Information Report (Fir)
alleging that on 12.03.2021, when his father, as a pillion rider, was proceeding towards
Chikkauligeri on the motorcycle bearing registration No. Ka-25/Em- 3266, a Cruiser vehicle
bearing registration No. Ka-29/A4956 came from the opposite direction at high speed and in a rash
and negligent manner, dashing against the motorcycle, resulting in his father sustaining accidental
injuries.

3. The police, after investigation, laid a charge sheet stating that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Cruiser vehicle by petitioner No.1, and petitioner No.2, the owner of the vehicle.
Taking exception to this, the present petition is filed.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5. In the FIR, the informant has categorically stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Cruiser Toofan vehicle.

However, in the statement recorded under NC:
2025:KHC-D:431 Section 161 Cr.P.C., the second respondent stated that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent riding of petitioner No.1.

During the course of the investigation, the two- wheeler/Cruiser vehicle belonging to petitioner No.2 was not implicated at the time of lodging the FIR, which clearly implies that the petitioners were implicated solely to claim compensation for the accidental injuries sustained by the father of respondent No.2.

Therefore, in the absence of credible Somanagouda Mahadevagouda ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82159108/
2 evidence to substantiate the allegations against the petitioners, continuing the criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of process of law.
